_what_this_is: Pre-change baseline for the phase11-ladder-contention slice, taken by the coordinator at the slice's own base so that any later claim of improvement is a comparison rather than an impression. Three consecutive pnpm verify:full invocations, each with a unique FITWAY_RUN_ID and its own disposable database, per-line timestamped.
note_on_base: This base does NOT contain the phase11-browser-debt repairs, which are preserved unintegrated on work/phase11-browser-debt-b01. The three registered assertions are therefore still load-sensitive here, by design.
headline: 3 of 3 full ladders went red at the base, each on a DIFFERENT assertion, and every one of those assertions is known to pass in isolation. No run failed twice on the same thing except phase3:82, which failed in two of three.

step_durations_seconds._comment: Measured between the ladder's own ==> step markers. A step that did not run because an earlier one failed is absent.

dominant_cost: The integration step is 399-476s, roughly 70-80 percent of the entire ladder, for 122 tests across 18 files. Every other step combined is under 90s. The browser step runs immediately after it.

corroboration_of_a_prior_finding: This baseline independently confirms (the refutation itself is recorded off-branch, see cross_branch_evidence_note) the phase11-browser-debt stage-1 refutation, which was analysis at the time and is now observation. The known-flaky register's entry browser-phase3-transient-state describes 'a transient-state timing assertion'. The stage-1 investigation refuted that from source and named line 82 - the closed heading, asserted before any transient - as a candidate red site. Line 82 is exactly what failed, twice, in runs taken by a different slice at a different commit with no knowledge of that prediction. The register entry's stated mechanism is wrong and its correction at closure is now evidence-backed rather than argued.
what_the_unit_step_shows: Unit tests passed 476/476 in all three baseline runs. The single unit-step failure previously observed at apps/web/src/hooks/use-owner-reporting.test.tsx:456 was on the phase11-browser-debt branch and did not reproduce here. It is therefore rarer than the browser and integration cases, not a per-run occurrence, and any mechanism proposed for this class must account for its rarity rather than assume uniform exposure.
boundaries_of_this_record: These are measurements, not a diagnosis. No runner configuration was read while producing them, so nothing here presupposes a cause. Attributing the pattern to a mechanism is stage 1's delegated work, and this record is its input.
raw_capture: Per-line timestamped transcripts retained outside the repository at the coordinator's scratchpad as baseline-b1.txt, baseline-b2.txt, baseline-b3.txt. They are tens of thousands of lines and are deliberately not committed.
